ov: A lobe-finned fish more closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to most fish. Known only from fossils and thought extinct for about 66 million years, it was found alive off South Africa in 1938. Two species survive, in the western Indian Ocean and off Indonesia.
wt: Average about 45 kg; up to 95 kg
rg: The western Indian Ocean from South Africa to Mozambique, the Comoros, Madagascar, Tanzania and Kenya; a second species lives off Sulawesi in eastern Indonesia.
df: Fish, hunted at night by drifting almost motionless; it may stand on its head to slurp prey from crevices.
fx: Females give birth to 5–25 live pups, which can fend for themselves straight away.
It spends the day in underwater lava caves and hunts nearby at night.
